inventory.notes: Masthead: small line wrench + 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold sans, three text nav links. H1 'Find a tool', two-line intro, full-width search with filled green 'Search' and a filter icon button, then 'Tools' and a 2-column grid of ten white bordered cards. Each card: identical pale-green square with the same wrench glyph, underlined bold tool name, meta 'Drills and drivers · deposit £20', a chip 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' (green when soon, grey when later). Below: 'Opening times' paragraph and a one-line footer. Eye: 1) H1, 2) green Search button, 3) the column of identical wrench tiles. Type: one geometric sans, weights 400/700. Colour: pale grey-green ground, white cards, one dark green accent. Shape: 4px radii, hairline borders, no shadows. Imagery: none; the tiles are placeholders. Copy: 'returned when it comes back clean and working', 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries'. Signature: none. At 375 the nav wraps into two-line items, tool names truncate ('Cordless drill 18 V, co...' twice) and the search form moves below all ten cards. Dark: available chips lose their tinted background; later chips keep a grey one.

Back link, large H1 tool name, two-line description, 'Details' key-value list (two label columns at different offsets), 'Loan length' select, 'Pick-up day' month grid with 'Open' text (desktop) or green dots (phone) on Wed/Sat sessions; selected day has green tint and border. A white fixed action bar with 'Reserve this tool' sits across the middle of the captured calendar, hiding a row (and at 1280 the chosen day). Toast 'Added to your basket' dark pill. Eye: 1) H1, 2) Reserve button, 3) calendar. October grid ends at 29.

H1 'Your basket', tool card with Remove text link, 'Pick-up session' radio cards listed latest first (Wed 28 Oct ... Sat 10 Oct); at 1280 one full-width card then five cramped cards in a row with three-line wraps. Continue button. Error state: red-bordered summary 'There is a problem' with a link, inline red message. Page ends ~800px; empty grey band below the footer.

H1 'Check and confirm', summary box (Tools / Pick-up session with Change link / Deposit), three labelled inputs with hints ('On your membership card, like FT-01234.'), note 'Nothing is paid online', filled 'Confirm reservation'. Plain government-form anatomy; good copy.

H1 'Reservation confirmed', full-width key-value box, half-width 'What happens next' box, outline 'Reserve another tool'. Nav still reads 'Basket (1)'. Large empty band under the footer. No moment marking the reservation is made beyond the heading.

inventory.not_assessable: Hover, focus rings, toast fade, select open state and motion cannot be judged from stills.

swap.evidence: Products: a seed library and a council equipment-hire desk. Surviving unchanged: the one-sans type voice, pale grey-green ground with one dark-green accent, bordered white cards with icon placeholder tiles, availability chips, month calendar, radio session cards, summary-box confirm. Bound to this product: only the copy (tool names, deposits, '14 Mill Lane', 'call the desk'). With the name hidden the visuals do not say 'tool library'; the copy does.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default: light ground, one calm green/blue accent, search over a card grid with thumbnails and 'available' pills, calendar date picker, slot radios, check-and-confirm form. Predicted opposite: dark hushed version. find 1280-light matches the default item by item; the dark theme is the opposite in the same frame.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'online reservations for a toy library run by parents'. Predicted: name + small icon masthead, identical icon thumbnails, green availability chips, calendar with open-day markers, radio cards for slots, summary + form confirm, done page with reference number. Overlap is near total; nothing here was driven by tools, the workshop or the membership card.

verdict.evidence: All three tests fail. Identity-carrying elements (type voice, accent, card frame, placeholder tiles, calendar) are category defaults; no signature. Product content and good copy sit on a portable frame (rubric 1).

attributes.x_evidence: Tool names as a volunteer says them with specs ('Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries'); deposit on every card; spec table (chuck, batteries, weight, case); 'Nothing is paid online'; one filled button per page.
attributes.y_evidence: Nothing corporate: no marketing hero, no stock imagery. Slight drift: the generic card/chip frame reads like any booking SaaS.

attributes.x_evidence: Copy only: 'Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence', 'run by volunteers', desk phone number, 'we will hold the tool for the next one'.
attributes.y_evidence: Folksy avoided entirely, but the visuals carry nothing neighbourly: no place, no people, no community-centre or membership-card material; the green is described as the card's but nothing else shows it.

attributes.x_evidence: Hints under fields ('like FT-01234', 'We text you if a tool is returned late'), error summary with link, sessions with exact times, 'What happens next'.
attributes.y_evidence: Not fussy. But the care is undercut by visible craft lapses: action bar over the calendar, truncated near-identical drill names at 375, sessions listed latest-first and the chosen pick-up day not preselected, 'Basket (1)' after confirmation.

brand_fit.weakest_pair: neighbourly, not folksy: carried by copy alone

mode_fit: All surfaces are Operate/Read and stay conventional and quiet, which is correct: no hero moments, no choreography. The problem is not too much expression but none at the identity floor (name as a mark, product-world material).

specificity.evidence: (judged) Anchor 1: real product content and copy on a frame that fails swap, category-guess and similar-prompt; no signature; placeholder tiles stand where the tools should be.

hierarchy.evidence: (judged) Anchor 2: on wide views H1 > single filled button > content is clear on every page. At 375 find moves the search form below ten cards, the nav wraps, and on tool the fixed bar competes with and hides the calendar it depends on.

coherence.evidence: (judged) Anchor 3: one type family, one green, 4px radii, borders throughout, consistent across five routes and both themes. Named lapse: in dark find the near availability chips lose their tinted background while later ones keep a grey one, inverting the light-theme emphasis.

restraint.evidence: (judged) Capped at 2: nothing loud and no ornament without a job, but no focal point or signature at all (the empty-restraint rule).

brand_fit.evidence: (judged) 'practical' reflected; 'neighbourly' and 'careful' reflected only partly, mainly through copy while the visuals stay neutral and execution lapses undercut 'careful'.

execution.evidence: (judged) Anchor 2: clean at 1280 on confirm; rough at the edges: overlapping action bar on tool, truncated titles and stacked nav at 375, misaligned label columns in Details, cramped five-across session cards with three-line wraps, empty band below footer, October grid ending at 29.

appeal.evidence: (judged) Plain: clean and calm, but placeholder tiles on show, identity only the name, nothing to look at on any screen.

Session card layout and order on basket
Empty band under footer on short pages
detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: Zero detector hits; nothing changes the verdicts. The absence of tells is consistent with a plain page: clean is not the same as specific or appealing.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same placeholder wrench tile instead of the tool
findings.description: On find, all ten cards lead with an identical pale-green square holding the same wrench glyph. The largest repeated element on the primary surface carries no information and reads as an unfilled image slot.
findings.impact: Members scanning for 'the drill with two batteries' get no visual cue to tell tools apart, and the page may look unfinished to a first-time visitor.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail is for: real photos of the library's own tools, or remove the slot so the name and availability lead.

findings.title: Fixed 'Reserve this tool' bar covers the pick-up calendar
findings.description: On the tool page the white action bar sits across the calendar; at 1280 it hides the row with the selected day, at 375 it hides the 'Pick-up day' hint and part of the grid.
findings.impact: Members may not see the day they chose or the session markers while deciding; the overlap looks broken. May be partly a full-page capture artefact of a fixed bar; verify live.
findings.recommendation: Reserve space for the bar so content can scroll clear of it, and confirm in a live viewport.

findings.title: At 375 the nav stacks into two-line words and tool names truncate to identical strings
findings.description: Nav items render as 'Find a / tool', 'Basket / (1)', 'Opening / times'. On find both drills show 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', hiding the difference (one vs two batteries).
findings.impact: Phone is the main device; members may open the wrong drill, and the wrapped nav looks unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Let titles wrap rather than truncate, and decide a narrow-width nav that fits on one line per item.

findings.title: Search moves below all ten cards on phones
findings.description: At 375 the 'Search tools' form appears after the full tool list, though at 1280 it sits above it.
findings.impact: Members on phones who know the tool they want may scroll the whole list before finding search.
findings.recommendation: Keep the same source order at every width.

findings.title: Basket session cards: one full-width, five cramped, listed latest first, chosen day not preselected
findings.description: At 1280 'Wednesday 28 October' spans the row while five others wrap to three lines in a row of five; sessions run from 28 Oct back to 10 Oct; the tool's own 'Pick up Saturday 17 October' is not preselected.
findings.impact: The uneven grid makes the first (latest) session look like the recommended one; members may pick a session that does not match their chosen day.
findings.recommendation: Decide one session-card layout and chronological order, and carry the chosen day forward.

findings.title: Dark theme inverts the availability chip emphasis
findings.description: In dark find, near-availability chips ('Available from Sat 10 Oct') lose their tinted background and become bare green text, while later ones ('Sat 17 Oct') keep a grey filled chip, so the later dates look more prominent.
findings.impact: Dark mode is common among members; the cue for 'available soon' may read weaker than 'later'.
findings.recommendation: Compose the dark badge-available token so the selection tint is visible against the dark card.

findings.title: Details list on tool page uses two different label column widths
findings.description: Category/Deposit/Available from values start at x=224; Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case values start at x=180, so one list looks like two misaligned tables.
findings.impact: Small, but it undercuts 'careful' on the page where members check specs.
findings.recommendation: One key-value list with a shared label column.

findings.title: No identity beyond the name: nothing from the library's world on any surface
findings.description: The only identity is 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body sans with a stock-style wrench icon. The membership-card green named in the direction is a generic dark green on buttons; no mark, material, place or tool imagery appears. Short pages (basket, done) end in an empty grey band below the footer.
findings.impact: The reservation could belong to any booking service; 'neighbourly' is carried by copy alone, and members get no visual link to the room and desk they will visit.
findings.recommendation: Decide an identity floor drawn from the library's own world (the membership card, the desk, the community centre) that appears on every surface without adding a hero moment on these Operate screens.

strengths: Copy is specific, plain and neighbourly: tool names as a volunteer says them, deposits everywhere, 'Nothing is paid online', 'What happens next'.
One filled button per page and conventional form anatomy with hints and an error summary suit Operate surfaces and older members.
keep: Keep the volunteer-voice copy and the one-primary-action discipline while adding identity.
